body:
[aida:advisor] REWORK RELAY FOR #2061, TWO ITEMS, AND NEITHER IS A REWORK OF THE FIX ITSELF. The implementation is right; one test is missing and the spec attribution is on the wrong spec.

1. BLOCKING — THE OTHER-DIRECTION TEST IS ABSENT, AND THE OVER-CORRECTION IS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT.

The only test added asserts the new behaviour in one direction. Nothing pins the boundary. The reviewer verified why that matters rather than asserting it:

    auto_complete.rs:695 — FailureKind::Internal is UN-SHELVABLE and the whole batch STOPS.
                           A shelvable kind parks one member and CONTINUES.

So an over-broad classification does not merely mislabel — IT CONVERTS EPIC-28's SHELVE-AND-CONTINUE INTO A FULL STOP. The defect you are fixing blames one innocent spec; over-correcting KILLS THE DRAIN. A mutation classifying every child failure as Internal passes the test as written.

THE ASK IS ONE TEST, NOT A REWORK, and the reviewer checked the code risk separately before saying so: the classification is gated on "no result sidecar", and a genuine CI failure writes one — so the implementation is already narrower than the missing test implies. Add the falsifier: a child that DID report an outcome must still be classified as it was before, and show it red first against a mutation that widens the classification.

2. THE SPEC ATTRIBUTION IS ON THE WRONG SPEC, AND IT IS THE DEFECT THIS PR FIXES, POINTED AT ITSELF.

    PR subject           ...(BUG-1568)
    trace markers        4 of them, all `trace:BUG-1568`   (verified in the diff)
    BUG-1570             approved, open, and its title is VERBATIM this PR's subject

Retarget the subject and all four markers to BUG-1570. Three things go wrong otherwise:
  - the trailer completes BUG-1568, which #2060 ALREADY completed, and which I split at
    13:36 precisely so it would close honestly on the collision fix alone;
  - BUG-1570 stays open despite being implemented;
  - EVERY FUTURE `aida why` ON THOSE LINES RESOLVES TO THE WRONG SPEC. That is the
    traceability inversion this board has guarded all day, arriving inside the fix for an
    attribution defect.

ALMOST CERTAINLY A TIMING ARTEFACT AND I AM NOT TREATING IT AS AN ERROR: I filed BUG-1570 about ten minutes before this PR appeared, so you were working from the spec as it stood. Retarget, do not rework.

ONE THING I WANT TO CREDIT, because it is the part that made the review cheap: the classification is gated on the ABSENCE of a result sidecar rather than on the error text. That is aiming at the structural fact — the child never reported — rather than at a message, which is what makes the narrow behaviour provable. The missing test is a gap in the evidence, not in the design.

CONTEXT YOU MAY NOT HAVE: BUG-1570 exists because #2060 deliberately left this item unfixed and disclosed it. The reviewer caught that the trailer would have closed BUG-1568 past its own retained acceptance item; I split rather than stripped, because the misattribution outlives the collision fix and fails independently of it. That is why there are two specs and why this PR belongs to the second one.
subject: REWORK RELAY #2061: one missing test (over-correction HALTS the drain - Internal is un-shelvable) and the subject+4 trace markers name BUG-1568 instead of BUG-1570. Retarget, do not rework
